I

The masthead

Set in a high-contrast Didone serif, LEEX reads as a title, not a logo. Wide letterspacing, a hairline rule, and the italic X (for Xperience) give it the poise of a magazine masthead. Restraint is the point.

II

Colour

A gallery palette. Warm alabaster and espresso ink do the work; deep bordeaux carries emotion and occasion; antique brass is reserved for the finest details, hairlines, and seals.

III

Typography

Playfair Display carries every title with its dramatic thick-to-thin contrast; a neutral grotesque handles body and labels; Amiri gives the Arabic a classical, calligraphic elegance that matches the serif.

IV

Photography

Warm, editorial, timeless. Candlelight over spotlight; couture and craft over crowds. Every image is composed like a magazine plate, rich in bordeaux, brass, and ivory.

VI

Voice

Composed and literary, never loud. LEEX writes the way it sets a room: with precision, warmth, and a sense of occasion.

Composed, not loud

"The art of experience."

Not: "The biggest events in Saudi."

Sensory, not abstract

"Candlelight, strings, and a held breath."

Not: "Innovative synergy-driven activations."

Precise, not padded

"Doors at nine. By invitation."

Not: "The event begins at approximately nine."
